lots.guide_summary: All AUD, no conversion. Same-series small Pro Hart dragonfly etchings sold at Gowans for $210, $230, $240 and $330 hammer in 2026 (4 SOLD, same or close). Other small Pro Hart AP/PP etchings sold at $130 to $220 hammer (category guide). 3 UNSOLD pairs (no last bid shown), including a framed Ant AP that passed in twice. No asking prices used. Overall the range is $130 to $330 hammer, about $160 to $400 all-in.
lots.working: Keep: lowest same-item SOLD within 24 months is $210 hammer (Gowans 427670, Aug 2026). 210 / 1.22 = 172.13, rounded down to $170 hammer ($207.40 all-in). Flip: likely resale about $220 hammer at Gowans (middle of 210, 230, 240). Less assumed 20% selling fees (vendor commission plus lotting and photo fees, not sourced) and $0 postage (sold locally) = $176. 176 / 2.44 = 72.1, rounded down to $70 hammer. Flipping leaves little margin, so this is a keep buy.
lots.confidence_reason: 'PRO HART' and 'A P' read in the photo, and four matching SOLD entries from the Gowans API, all within 24 months, with lot photos checked. Authenticity is not verified (Pro Hart prints are sometimes faked), and the comparable sales carry the same risk.
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped. Corrections: 427670 upgraded from category guide to same item (photo shows the same dragonfly series); 384144 lot id added for the $130 PP. Researcher's Gowans figures checked against the API and all match. Gowans URLs are API search URLs, the lot ids identify the lots. lots.question_for_armitage: Is there anything on the back (gallery label, certificate, Broken Hill provenance)? Is the signature in pencil, and is there a visible plate mark? Any foxing or damage to the frame or glass? What is the '777' tag in the frame?

lots.what_it_is: Queen Anne style figured walnut toilet (dressing table) mirror: arched cushion-moulded frame with carved shell cresting and a foxed, crackled plate, on square uprights over a bombe base with three small shaped drawers above one long drawer, ogee bracket feet, brass drop handles. Most likely a 19th or early 20th century revival piece; a genuine early 18th century example cannot be ruled out from the photos.

lots.question_for_armitage: Can you check the drawer construction (hand-cut or machine dovetails) and the back of the mirror plate, and whether the veneer is solid walnut or a later finish? Height and width? Does the mirror swing and hold position, and are there veneer losses or repairs?
